p:cNvPr.descr: A pie chart that represents the durations (in hours) of the four stages of the eukaryotic cell cycle. Starting from the top left is G2, which lasts 3-4 hours and is shaded green, followed by the M phase, which lasts 1 hour and is shaded purple. In the G2 Phase, there is no DNA synthesis, and RNA and protein synthesis continue. In the M phase, mitosis (nuclear division) and cytokinesis (cell division) yield two daughter cells. Next, is G1, which is shaded blue and lasts 6-12 hours, followed by the S phases, which is shaded yellow and lasts 6-8 hours. Before the G1 phase, terminally differentiated cells withdraw from the cell cycle (GO Phase) GO is represented by reversible arrows. A cell returning from GO enters at early G1, and in the G1 phase, RNA and protein synthesis occur, but there is no DNA synthesis. In S phase,DNA synthesis doubles the amount of DNA in the cell, and RNA and protein are also synthesized. The size of the sections are dependent on how long the phase lasts, so G1 is the largest, followed by S, the, G2, and finally, M.

p:cNvPr.descr: A graph of the variations in the activities of specific CDKs during the cell cycle in animals. On the horizontal axis is time, and on the vertical axis is kinase activity. There are no markers. At the top of the graph, from left to right, from largest to smallest in size, the sections are labeled based on their color; G1 (blue), S phase (yellow), G2 (green), M (purple), and a lighter G1. Three lines are shown on the graph. A blue line, labeled, "Cyclin E-CDK2" forms a bell curve starting toward the end of the first G1 and ending in the middle of the yellow S phase. A green line starts at a point before the endpoint of the blue line, and increases across the green bar (G2) about halfway up, then decreases and has an endpoint half way through the purple bar (M) on the horizontal line. Finally, the red line starts right before the end of the green bar on the horizontal line and peaks almost at the top of the purple bar. It then decreases and has an endpoint on the horizontal line, a few units to the right of the green line's endpoint.
